summary: 41-year-old smoker, not lactating, with a third episode of a painful periareolar abscess. Periductal mastitis: ultrasound + aspiration, antibiotics covering anaerobes, smoking cessation, and imaging to exclude an underlying carcinoma once settled; recurrent disease may need duct excision.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Painful swelling next to the left nipple again
inputs.hpi: Third episode in 18 months of a painful swelling beside the left nipple. Previous two were drained. Not breastfeeding (children 12 and 15). Smokes 20 a day. Some cheesy discharge from the nipple.

exam.other: Left breast: 2.5 cm tender fluctuant periareolar swelling at 4 o'clock with erythema; slit-like nipple retraction; scar from previous drainage. No axillary nodes.

imaging.name: USS left breast
imaging.result: Periareolar 2.2 cm collection communicating with a dilated subareolar duct.

surgicalHistory: Incision and drainage left periareolar abscess x2

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Recurrent non-lactational periareolar abscess (periductal mastitis) in a smoker
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Recurrent non-lactational periareolar breast abscess (periductal mastitis), smoker. Ultrasound-guided aspiration, co-amoxiclav (anaerobic cover), smoking cessation; imaging after resolution; consider total duct excision when quiescent.

mustRankTopK.knownGapNote: PANE top 3 = cholecystitis, fibroadenoma, fibrocystic change: only breast_lump was extracted (no redness/pain/discharge feature from chips). PANE: unlisted features count at DEFAULT_SENSITIVITY 0.30 for every disease and there is no false-positive term, so high-prior abdominal diseases (cholecystitis 0.15, GORD 0.12, PUD 0.10; male inguinal hernia x5) outrank the organ-specific disease after a single non-abdominal feature.

mustInclude.knownGapNote: The breast_abscess protocol has no non-lactational (periductal mastitis) branch: no smoking cessation or duct excision.

mustExclude.note: Breastfeeding advice is irrelevant (not lactating): a sign that the plan does not adapt to the history.

guideline.name: Best practice diagnostic guidelines for patients presenting with breast symptoms (ABS / RCR, Department of Health)
guideline.section: Triple assessment (clinical examination, age-appropriate imaging, needle biopsy); imaging by age; nipple discharge; breast infection; breast pain
guideline.citation: Willett AM, Michell MJ, Lee MJR (eds). Best practice diagnostic guidelines for patients presenting with breast symptoms. London: Department of Health / Association of Breast Surgery; 2010.

rationale: Permutation: non-lactational, smoker, recurrent. Tests that the plan adapts (anaerobic cover, smoking, exclude carcinoma, duct excision) rather than repeating the lactational template.
